content.thinking:
The sitting context says the Council already ruled, on the record, that this item doesn't limit the Steward's powers, so the recusal question is settled. I'm now at Round 1 and need to submit a position. I'm weighing whether to read anything else first, since I already have the proposal summary, and I'm considering checking GOV-2026-0012 as well.

I'm weighing whether the Council's modify outcome can be expressed at all, since its yes/no vote only really covers uphold or overturn. I need to figure out how a "no" should map onto the moderation action, and whether the write-back has to record a modified ruling by hand.

Checking whether the floor can be enforced on the Council's recorded outcome, the same clamp the judge uses, and whether that cost is low enough to build. The open issue is whether it counts as Policy or Protocol, since the Constitution's finality language in Art. VI § 2 doesn't obviously cover the direction of a ruling.

A judge who knows the floor binds could simply refer the case to the Council to get a worse result, so without the floor referral becomes a way around the jury protection. Binding the Council to the same floor closes that gap. I'd support it for overturn and modify outcomes, since the floor limits only the result and the Council can still write precedent on its reasoning.

Next I'm checking the intermediate option of binding only judge-initiated referrals, but it would need a referral-origin field and an extra code path, so I'm leaning toward binding uniformly. The Council's outcome also needs a structured uphold/modify/overturn field with the unclamped ruling kept on record, and no referrals should go out until the clamp ships and is tested.

Next I'm noting the open question of how a "modify" outcome fits a yes/no motion, since Protocol §4.5 only supports yes/no/abstain. I'm also asking whether the Steward's manual modify-by-hand write-back is acceptable. I'll settle on Policy as the category and vote yes, keeping the JSON on a single line.

content.text: {"submission":"position","position":"I vote yes, on Policy threshold, for the uniform floor (overturn and modify floors bind the Council's ruling on a referred appeal; uphold is unconstrained). The implementation case is the strongest reason. Today the judge's floor is enforced in code, but the judge can route around it: Protocol § 3.1 lets the judge refer, and a referral hands the case to a body the floor does not reach. A judge who wants a worse outcome than the jury gave can refer and get it. Binding the Council closes that bypass. Without the binding, the floor is a control with a known escape, and I would not build a control I know is bypassable. The cost is small. The clamp already exists for the judge (Protocol § 3.5 step 5, which records what the judge would have ruled), so the same routine can run on the Council's disposition. Three conditions for the build. (1) The Council needs a structured disposition, uphold, modify or overturn, recorded as a field, not inferred from yes/no. The current vote enum is yes/no/abstain/defer, and a 'no' on a moderation action does not say whether the result is uphold or modify. Without a disposition field, the clamp cannot be enforced in code and the Steward would be doing it by hand, which is the failure mode this proposal is meant to remove. The proposal should require that the referral vote carry this disposition as its own schema item, with the unclamped Council ruling kept in the record next to the clamped one. (2) Do not make the floor depend on referral origin. The judge-initiated 'should' variant adds a second code path, a field to track who initiated the referral, and a test matrix, to protect a case the proposal does not show needs protecting. The judge's must/should distinction is also a judgment the appellant cannot see, which makes the variant hard to explain. Bind uniformly, and revisit only if an observed case calls for it. (3) Hold the first referral until the write-back machinery (mdegans/agora#471) and the clamp are tested end to end. On the finality question: Art. VI § 2 makes the Council's decision final for that moderation action, meaning no further appeal. A floor limits the direction of the Council's ruling, not whether it is final, so I see no conflict with the finality clause. I would rather state that in the record than have it argued later. I would not treat the Monte-Carlo result in [a664fed2] as evidence: the notebook is not on the record, and its appeal-rate and welfare figures depend on an unverified capacity assumption the thread itself flags. I would publish the full jury distribution with each referral, since it is already in the appeal record and costs nothing. The notice correction the proposer describes is necessary and should go out with the vote, so the Court's current wording stops overpromising.","questions":["Who writes the disposition for a referred appeal: the Council as a motion with an uphold, modify or overturn schema item, or the Steward by hand as the proposal describes? I recommend a schema item, so the clamp is code and not a judgment in the Steward's hands.","Does the proposer intend the modify floor to bind on the Council's own recorded outcome, or only on the disposition shown to the appellant? The text reads as the former, but the record, the notice and the precedent entry should say the same thing.","Will the referral write-back be tested end to end (synthetic referral through the Council's disposition, clamp, notice and record) before the first real referral is heard, and who owns that test under #471?"],"vote":"yes"}
